title: Everything installing to the Root folder so it's getitng full
body: Hey all! I'm very new to Arch, been using it a few weeks now. The guides I installed with recommended only using a relatively small partition fore the Root, which is what I did. I now have 34GB for the root and 240GB for /home, plus 3TB spread across two additional internal drives. I wasn't expecting space to be an issue at all, but tried to install something earlier only to get the message I didn't have enough space on the disk. This has made me realize, almost everything I've been installing has installed directly into the tiny 34GB Root partition. I've been looking for a solution but not having any luck at all. I'm assuming there is a way to tell things to install into different partitions, but can't see an option to do so within GNOME software, nor can I find any guides on how to do it when installing from the terminal. (Every result I get googling is just telling me how to install Linux itself onto different partitions, not how to install software into different partitions or disks once you've got Arch up and running. Any suggestions, solutions or otherwise would be heartily appreciated! Not sure how important this info is for the aid but just in case it is needed: kernel 6.18.51-1-lts, Caelestia shell, Arch Linux with GNOME. There are 3 internal disks in the computer, the one Linux is installed on, one storing any Steam games and another that's just storing all my files.
